name: Eastern Plaguelands
summary: The Eastern Plaguelands represent the devastated heart of the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, suffocated under Scourge blight, toxic mists, and corrupted fungal growths. Stratholme looms in the north as the undead power base in the region, while the zealous Scarlet Crusade entrenches in the east. Amid the nightmare, Light's Hope Chapel stands as a resolute, neutral sanctuary for anyone brave enough to fight back.

sections.title: A Land in Ruin
sections.body: Once known as the fertile Eastweald, this region was the agricultural spine of northern Lordaeron, anchored by the great metropolis of Stratholme and prosperous towns like Darrowshire and Corin's Crossing. During the Third War, Prince Arthas purged Stratholme after discovering its grain supply had been laced with the Plague of Undeath. Following the kingdom's collapse, the Scourge's dark magic ran unchecked. The soil turned brown and rotten, ordinary flora warped into colossal mushrooms, and an eerie orange mist settled across the valleys.

sections.title: A War on Three Fronts
sections.body: Stratholme serves as the southern seat of Scourge authority in Lordaeron, commanded by Baron Rivendare under the direction of the lich Kel'Thuzad. Defying the undead from the southeast is the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, which has fortified the town of Tyr's Hand and assaults Stratholme's scarlet bastions. Their dogmatic hatred extends beyond the dead to any living traveler who crosses their borders. To the north, the Mossflayer forest trolls of Zul'Mashar wage their own isolated, desperate campaigns, caught in the crossfire of the greater conflict.

sections.title: Bastions of the Living
sections.body: Survival in the Eastern Plaguelands requires careful footing. The neutral Argent Dawn operates out of Light's Hope Chapel in the far east, offering a safe haven, essential supplies, and flight routes to both Alliance and Horde champions. Beyond the chapel, the two factions actively clash over four strategic ruined towers—Crown Guard, Eastwall, Northpass, and Plaguewood—wrestling for area-wide tactical dominance to bolster their fighters against the undead horrors.

faq.q: What caused the sky and trees to look so sick?
faq.answer: The landscape suffers from the concentrated effects of the Cult of the Damned's Plague of Undeath. Left unchecked after the Third War, the foul necromantic magic blighted the earth, mutated local wildlife, choked the atmosphere in an unnatural orange smog, and transformed natural forests into grotesque fungal groves like the Plaguewood.

faq.q: Where can I find a safe haven or flight path here?
faq.answer: Light's Hope Chapel, located along the eastern edge of the zone, is the main sanctuary. Maintained by the Argent Dawn, it provides flight paths connecting to Undercity, Ironforge, Chillwind Camp, and the Hinterlands, welcoming both Alliance and Horde travelers.

faq.q: Who controls the city of Stratholme?
faq.answer: Stratholme is divided by ongoing warfare. The majority of the burning ruins are ruled by the Scourge under Baron Rivendare, serving Kel'Thuzad. However, the Scarlet Crusade maintains an aggressive garrison within the western district, waging a relentless and bloody siege against the undead forces.

faq.q: Why is the Scarlet Crusade hostile to outside adventurers?
aliases: why does scarlet crusade attack me
faq.answer: Following the fall of Lordaeron and the fracturing of the Silver Hand, the Scarlet Crusade succumbed to rampant zealotry and paranoia. Convinced that all outsiders harbor the taint of the plague or consort with the undead, they attack any non-members who approach their strongholds, such as Tyr's Hand.

faq.q: What happened to the town of Darrowshire?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Scourge forces led by the death knight Marduk the Black and the ghoul Horgus the Ravager assaulted the town. Although paladin Davil Crokford and Captain Joseph Redpath fought valiantly, Redpath's soul was corrupted by necromancy, turning him into an instrument of slaughter against his own people. The town now lies in haunted ruins.

faq.q: Why are Alliance and Horde fighting over the ruined towers?
faq.answer: Scattered across the zone are four ruined Lordaeron watchtowers: Crown Guard, Eastwall, Northpass, and Plaguewood. Both factions contend for their control to claim strategic defensive outposts and area-wide tactical boons that aid their forces against the surrounding undead.

angles.text: The fallen realm of Lordaeron holds profound tragedy for the Silver Hand, from the site of Arthas's dark turning in Stratholme to the valiant last stand at Light's Hope Chapel.
The Eastern Plaguelands represent both the birthplace of the Scourge menace and a vital frontline where the Forsaken strike back against their former masters and the Scarlet zealots.
For the Alliance, venturing into the Plaguelands is a solemn pilgrimage to reclaim and honor the devastated remnants of their former northern allies.
This blighted region is one of the exceptionally rare places to gather volatile, high-tier herbs like Arthas' Tears, Plaguebloom, and Black Lotus.
Veins of Truesilver, Mithril, and Rich Thorium are embedded across the corrupted hillsides and dangerous Scourge-infested valleys.
